Management Plan
2026
DIRECTORATE-GENERAL FOR EDUCATION,
YOUTH, SPORT AND CULTURE
1

PART 1. Introduction
The Directorate-General for Education, Youth, Sport and Culture (DG EAC) designs and delivers
EU policies and programmes that empower people, develop talents and strengthens societies
through education, culture, youth, sport and fairness between generations. DG EAC supports
high-quality and inclusive education and training systems, attractive and sustainable research
careers, cross-border mobility and solidarity, vibrant cultural and creative sectors, active youth
engagement as well as a values-based sport model as essential pillars of the European project.
DG EAC’s work supports excellence, innovation, inclusiveness, intergenerational fairness and
convergence across Member States and contributes to a resilient, democratic, competitive and
prosperous European Union.
Strategic planning and programming is the cornerstone of the Commission’s performance
management framework. The Commission’s strategic plan for 2025-2029 translates the
political priorities set in the Political Guidelines of President von der Leyen into general
objectives. This process ensures institutional coherence, enhances accountability, and aligns the
actions of all Commission services with the strategic vision of the mandate.
Within this framework, each Commission service has developed a strategic outlook for
2025-2029 in its Management plan 2025. This outlook defines a set of multiannual objectives
and indicators to measure progress towards their achievement. These will be used for planning
and reporting on performance throughout the period.
The 2026 management plan sets out what the Directorate-General for Education, Youth,
Sport and Culture intends to deliver this year to contribute to these multiannual objectives (part
2). It also describes how the Directorate-General for Education, Youth, Sport and Culture will
contribute to the common objective of building a modern and sustainable public administration
(part 3). The main outputs with their indicators and targets are presented in Annexes 1 and 2.
The chart below illustrates the performance framework for DG EAC.
3

PART 2. Delivering on the Commission’s
priorities in 2026
General Objective 1 - A new plan for Europe’s
sustainable prosperity and competitiveness
Specific Objective 1.1 – Steering policies and managing
programmes that support Europe's competitiveness through
high-quality, inclusive and future-proof education policies,
equipping people with relevant skills and competences for
Europe’s green and digital transitions
In 2026, DG EAC will continue placing the Union of Skills and the European Education Area
at the heart of its work to strengthen Europe’s competitiveness and preparedness. This work
will directly support the implementation of the Competitiveness Compass and the EU’s
Preparedness Strategy.
As part of the Education package of Q3 2026, the 2030 Roadmap on the future of
Digital Education and Skills, will promote equal access to education for all, in the age of AI
through a robust EU digital education ecosystem, with long-term partnerships with EU-based
EdTech and independently developed European solutions. This objective is more relevant than
ever in the current global political context, as autonomy and sovereignty of digital solutions,
including those for education, are becoming more important.
The EU Teachers and Trainers Agenda will help Member States improve teachers’ working
conditions, training and career prospects. A dedicated EU analysis of the OECD Teaching and
Learning International Survey (TALIS) report on the view of teachers on their working conditions
will be published in Q1 2026 in support of the EU Teachers and Trainers Agenda.
As part of the Union of Skills’ governance, DG EAC will contribute, taking into account political
guidance, to the establishment of a European Skills High Level Board for more agile policy-
making, and a European Skills Intelligence Observatory for evidence-base intelligence to
make education and skills policies future proof. The EU-27 recommendation on human
capital under the European Semester will help addressing the most pressing and strategic
decisions needed to boost skills and competitiveness. Closely linked to competitiveness and the
broader socio-economic policy landscape, under the European Semester, DG EAC will
contribute to the 27 country reports, country-specific recommendations and monitor the
completion of a significant number of reforms and investments in education and culture under
the Recovery and Resilience Facility, which will close in 2026. The work on the European
Education Area will be stepped up under the second (2026-2030) cycle of the strategic
5

framework. European cooperation will focus on revised strategic priorities and progress will be
monitored through the reviewed EU-level targets. Skill intelligence and sound evidence will
be reinforced by DG EAC's contributions to the European Skills Observatory and the annual
Education and Training Monitor, which assesses progress towards achieving objectives and
EU-level targets.
In the context of AI, in Q1 2026 DG EAC will launch four sets of guidelines developed
under the Digital Education Action Plan 2021-2027, on one hand the revised guidelines on
Artificial Intelligence and on Tackling Disinformation, on the other hand, new guidelines on
High-Quality Informatics and on Digital Education Content. In Q2 2026, DG EAC will launch
the final version of the AI literacy framework, developed together with the OECD, to support
education systems to build AI readiness. The framework will offer a common understanding
of what it means to be AI literate, what the main building competences are and how to
support teachers to foster them in the classroom. This framework will also inform the PISA
2029 assessment, providing a measurable way to follow its impact on education, and its
mainstreaming in education systems will be a crucial task going forward.
In 2026, DG EAC will continue the implementation of the STEM Education Strategic Plan. In
Q1 2026, DG EAC will launch the STEM Education executive panel. The panel will contribute to
intelligence production on strategic issues in STEM education, such as how to make it more
attractive and bring it closer to the labour market. The STEM Education Strategic Plan will also
roll out measures to strengthen STEM talent and EU innovation capacity, including STEM
Education Foundries (Erasmus+ Alliances for Innovation) promoting entrepreneurship, IP
management, and student start-ups. It will also support new educational programmes and
training in quantum computing, AI, micro-credentials, and a European Degree for Engineers.
A key focus will be on inclusiveness and female participation in STEM, aiming for 1 million
girls and women in STEM by 2028, starting with the Girls Go STEM initiative in 2026, an
initiative implemented by the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT).
The EIT and its Knowledge and Innovation Communities (KICs) will continue to develop
entrepreneurial skills and support the green and digital transitions. Through the Union of Skills
and the STEM Plan, the EIT will train 1 million learners by 2028 for green and digital
transitions, for example through the STEM Tech Talent Induction. The EIT Higher Education
Institutions initiative support universities’ knowledge transfer and strengthen ties with
European Universities alliances.
DG EAC will continue to develop and implement the joint European degree label and
prepare for a fully-fledged European degree, in cooperation with Member States through
the “Policy Lab” and the “European Degree Forum”. In 2026, guidelines for coherent
implementation across Europe will be finalised, allowing higher education institutions to award
the label from mid-2026. Two calls will support this work: one for European degree pathway
projects and another for exploratory actions. An additional exploratory action will pilot
Erasmus+ scholarships in critical fields, providing evidence for the 2028–2034 programme
design. In the youth field, informal and non-formal learning, youth participation, and
volunteering will continue to foster skills for employability, life, and active citizenship.
6

Building on its strong track-record in this respect, Erasmus+ will continue contributing to
promoting EU’s competitiveness by enhancing citizens’ skills and to equipping people for the
twin transitions, through supporting mobility and cooperation in education, including informal
and non-formal education, training, youth and sport.
Erasmus+ and the European Solidarity Corps will continue supporting projects that protect
the environment, promote sustainability, and encourage behavioural changes in consumption
and lifestyles. The SALTO Resource Centre on Green Transition will enhance the green
dimension of both programmes by sharing good practices, building National Agencies’ capacity,
and providing eco-tips for participants and organisations. Both programmes will also promote
the effective use of digital tools to strengthen learners’ digital skills and organisational
readiness. The SALTO Digital Resource Centre will continue implementing the digital
transformation priority, acting as a hub between policy and practice to improve digital
education and youth work. The digital opportunity traineeships (DOTs) will continue to be
supported, boosting digital skills for VET and higher education students and recent graduates in
relation to their fields of study as well as enriched digital pedagogical skills for school, VET,
Higher Education and adult learning staff.
The political negotiations will be running in 2026 on the future generation of the EU
programmes with a view to their adoption for the post-2027 cycle. Building on the
Commission’s MFF proposal (Erasmus+, AgoraEU, Horizon Europe), DG EAC will work on the
design of investment pathways for the European Universities alliances, to allow for
comprehensive funding schemes which support the alliances in all their dimensions, including
research and strategic skills development. A report on options for a future legal basis for
European Universities alliances will be delivered in 2026.
Specific Objective 1.2 - Steering policies and managing
programmes that reinforce cutting-edge education and
Europe’s research talent pipeline and innovation ecosystems
In 2026, the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) will mark 30 years of promoting
research excellence, supporting researchers’ careers, and strengthening European
competitiveness. Anniversary activities will run throughout the year, including a high-level event
in Q2 2026, at the historic Solvay Library with College members, political, industry and
academic leaders, Nobel Laureates and MSCA fellows. The event will celebrate the MSCA’s
legacy and discuss the future of European research and talent attraction.
2026 will also see the launch of the MSCA Choose Europe for Science pilot, enabling
selected organisations to recruit researchers who will benefit from excellent conditions and
long-term career prospects. The pilot will pave the way for a 2027 scale-up within the broader
Choose Europe initiative.
The MSCA will continue its schools’ outreach through Science is Wonderful! (March), the
European Researchers’ Night (September), and Researchers at Schools throughout the
year. The annual MSCA Conference will take place under the Irish Presidency in November.
7

Under the supervision of DG EAC, the EIT will continue to foster competitiveness, bridging the
gap between entrepreneurial education, skills development, research, and business. In close
collaboration with its 10 KICs (including the new KIC on water, marine and maritime that is
expected to be launched in 2026), the EIT community will continue to serve as a catalyst for
innovation-based growth, narrowing the innovation gap in Europe, and bringing innovative
products and services to the market. The EIT will further contribute to reducing Europe’s
innovation divide through the Regional Innovation Scheme.
Under Horizon Europe Cluster 2, DG EAC will co-chair implementation of the 2026–27 work
programme with DG RTD and DG EMPL. Planned for 2026 are 9 calls under Democracy and
Governance, 7 under Cultural Heritage, 10 under Social and Economic Transformations,
including a major call for the European Partnership on Social Transformations and
Resilience.
General Objective 3 - Supporting people, and
strengthening our societies and our social
models
Specific Objective 3.1 - Steering policies and managing
programmes that support inclusive and quality education to
empower young people’s social engagement and solidarity
across the EU, strengthening intergenerational fairness and
cohesion
Promoting inclusive high-quality education and training for all is at the heart of DG EAC’s work
in implementing the European Education Area and the Union of Skills. This work is
mutually reinforced when connected to the broader social inclusion and equality policy
initiatives, in particular the ones adopted at the end of 2025 and planned for 2026 (e.g.
LGBTIQ Equality Strategy, Anti-Racism Strategy, Gender Equality Strategy, Anti-poverty
strategy, Fair labour mobility package, strengthening the European Child Guarantee). The
equality mainstreaming work plan of DG EAC, instrumental in coordinating this work for all EAC
policies and funding programmes, as well as human resources, will be renewed in 2026 for the
period 2026-2030.
A key deliverable in 2026 will be the Education Package, which will encompass the Basic
Skills Support Scheme and the European School Alliances under General Objective 3. The Basic
Skills Support Scheme will support effective interventions at school level, and target children
and young people who struggle to acquire basic skills in line with the wider notion set out in the
Action Plan on Basic Skills, i.e. literacy, mathematics, science, digital skills as well as citizenship
skills and civic knowledge. The European School Alliances will enhance cross-border cooperation
and mobility between schools across Europe, and offer more structured, long-term
8

collaboration between schools and school authorities, leading to more open and higher quality
education systems in Europe. In this context, the EU Teachers and Trainers Agenda will help
Member States improve teachers’ working conditions, training and career prospects.
As part of the implementation of the Action Plan on Basic Skills, DG EAC will support
Member States in their efforts to improve the level of basic skills with the Peer Counselling
Cluster on Basic Skills. Other actions announced in the Action Plan on Basic Skills will also be
launched in 2026, including the EU Literacy Coalition.
The Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps programmes will continue to support learning
opportunities for all, improving educational equity and increasing participation rates of people
with fewer opportunities through flexible and simple participation formats, tailor-made help
and financial support. The programmes will, among others, foster the development of basic
skills, critical thinking and media literacy, and promote intergenerational fairness and learning.
They will foster a culture of solidarity, care and understanding among citizens, especially the
youngest generations. Non-formal and informal learning and training activities are essential to
reducing social divergences, preventing intolerance and promoting common values.
The Learning Lab on Investing in Quality Education and Training will keep promoting and
supporting the evaluation of the quality and relevance of investment in education and training.
DG EAC will also publish its annual report on Investment in Education in the EU.
The Strategy on Intergenerational Fairness will be adopted in Q1 2026. It will aim to
ensure that decisions taken today do no harm to future generations and that there is increased
solidarity and engagement between people of different ages. It will seek to map out how DG
EAC can strengthen solidarity between generations and ensure that interests of future
generations are respected throughout out policy and law making. DG EAC will work horizontally
with DGs on the development and implementation of the strategy and will raise awareness on
intergenerational fairness in its communication activities and aim to mainstream the topic
within the Commission. It will also work on integrating intergenerational fairness in education,
culture, youth and sport policies.
Specific Objective 3.2 - Steering policies and managing a
programme that safeguards and promotes cultural diversity
and heritage, fostering sustainable and innovative cultural
and creative sectors, contributing to the Culture Compass
In the field of cultural policy, 2026 will be the first year of implementation of the Culture
Compass for Europe, the new overarching strategic framework for cultural policy at EU level.
The Commission Communication on the Culture Compass for Europe adopted in November
2025 is accompanied by a proposal for a Joint Declaration highlighting interinstitutional and
political commitment to the guiding principles underlying cultural policy cooperation at the EU
level. In 2026, the Joint Declaration should be discussed and endorsed jointly by the European
Commission, the Council and the European Parliament.
9

In parallel, the Commission will launch preparations to implement some of the flagship actions
presented in the Culture Compass. These will include, inter alia, launching consultations to
shape the announced AI strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors; strengthening data
collection on the cultural and creative sectors in view of establishing the new Cultural Data Hub;
organising a structured dialogue with stakeholders.
2026 will also mark the end of the current cycle of policy cooperation with EU Member States
under the EU Work Plan for Culture 2023-2026. The Commission will present a report on its
implementation by mid-2026. Work with Member States on the preparation of the next
multiannual Work Plan for Culture will start in parallel. Among the final deliverables under the
current Work Plan, the group of Member States’ experts on the roles of libraries in society is
expected to publish its report, and the Commission will present the results of the study on the
discoverability of diverse European cultural content online.
Creative Europe will continue to strengthen cross-border cultural cooperation, social inclusion,
and societal resilience, integrating digital and green priorities. Targeted support will be provided
to people with disabilities, minorities, and marginalised groups. The programme will further
promote intercultural dialogue and help safeguard European cultural heritage, building on
existing activities and integrating reinforced actions such as the next phase of Culture Moves
Europe and the renewed European Authors Day. Collectively, these actions will contribute to the
implementation of the Culture Compass and to a more cohesive, inclusive and diverse European
cultural space.
Specific Objective 3.3 – Developing policies and managing
programme funds to develop an effective European
dimension of sport, promoting healthy lifestyles, social
participation, while promoting and reinforcing an inclusive,
competitive and values-based European Sport Model
In 2026, DG EAC will continue to promote the European dimension of sport, reflecting the
importance of the role of sport as an anchor in society from an education and social
perspective, thus fostering sport’s increasingly valuable role as a European asset –
economically, socially, politically and culturally.
DG EAC will prepare the Commission Communication: “A Strategic Vision for Sport in
Europe: Reinforcing the European Sport Model”, which will also be guided by the insights
gathered from the public consultation organised in the second half of 2025.
In 2026, the Commission will sign its fourth Arrangement for Cooperation with UEFA. This
partnership will continue a productive dialogue with a major sport organisation in Europe,
engaging in concrete cooperation activities, contributing to the implementation of EU policy
objectives such as the promotion of an inclusive, value-based model of sport, good governance
in sport, protection of minors, human rights, gender equality, and health-enhancing physical
activity.
10

In 2026 the new Special Eurobarometer on Sport will be published as follow-up to the last
publication of 2022. The survey will help to inform sport policy and provide important input for
the review of the Council Recommendation on Health-Enhancing Physical Activity.
In spring 2026, DG EAC will organise its annual EU Sport Forum in Cyprus. The event will
gather more than 400 sport stakeholders across Europe to discuss key sport topics, such as
sport governance, athletes’ rights and wellbeing and the European Sport Model.
The 2026 #BeActive campaign and the European Week of Sport (EWoS) – with thousands of
activities taking place across Europe between 23 and 30 September 2026 - will continue to
raise citizens’ awareness of the joy and benefits of sport and will advocate the contribution of
sport and physical activity to enhance physical and mental health.
Moreover, the enhanced #BeActive EU Sport Awards, which in 2025 integrated the former
#BeInclusive EU Sport Awards and #BeActive Awards, will continue to increase the visibility of
exemplary sport projects and the organisations behind them. The #BeActive EU Sport Awards
ceremony will be held in Brussels in June 2026.
Throughout 2026, DG EAC will continue its work with the World Health Organisation and
Member States in view of preparing a proposal for a review of the Council Recommendation on
Health-Enhancing Physical Activity (HEPA).
DG EAC will continue to support Member States in the works of the two Open Methods of
coordination groups (OMC groups) on “Promoting athletes’ rights within the context of good
governance in sport” and “Fight against hate speech in sport’ launched in 2025.
The Erasmus+ sport programme remains the key instrument to boost sport’s inclusive and
values-based role, including at the grassroots sport and the international level. It plays a pivotal
role in promoting sport and physical activity across Europe through various initiatives designed
to tackle societal and sport-related challenges. Erasmus+ sport cooperation partnerships,
capacity building and sport events will enable organisations to develop and implement joint
activities focused on addressing sport policy priorities such as promoting sport and physical
activity for all, addressing threats to the integrity of sport, supporting dual careers for athletes,
improving governance, fostering tolerance and social inclusion, etc.
Specific Objective 3.4 - Supporting international cooperation
in education, culture, youth, sport, and to enhance
international partnerships, promote EU values and address
shared global challenges
In 2026, DG EAC will reinforce its contribution to the EU enlargement process, with a sharp
focus on Ukraine, Moldova and the Western Balkans including through the organisation of an
Education Ministerial meeting with enlargement countries. DG EAC will also hold the EU-Ukraine
High-Level Dialogue on Education, and, together with DG EMPL, prepare the second EU-Moldova
High-Level Dialogue on Education and EMPL policies. In parallel, DG EAC will engage in the
11

preparation of the 2026 Enlargement report as well as in annual committee and sub-
committee meetings, and other high-level events such as the Ukraine Recovery Conference.
Also, DG EAC will support the preparation of those candidate countries and potential candidates
not yet associated to Erasmus+ for future association, so that they can fully participate in and
benefit from all actions of the programme.
DG EAC will continue supporting Ukraine via the implementation of the programmes under its
remit using their in-built flexibility. In addition, support to Ukrainian culture and heritage will
remain a top priority, especially through the Team Europe Approach.
DG EAC will support DG MENA in implementing key actions under the first pillar of the new
Pact for the Mediterranean. In 2026, DG EAC will organise the first-ever Ministerial Meeting
on Higher Education under the Union for the Mediterranean, aiming to create a platform to
coordinate education policies and initiatives.
Together with DG EMPL, DG EAC will also hold the first High-Level Education and Skills Dialogue
with India, bringing together policymakers, quality assurance authorities, education institutions
and training providers. In 2026, DG EAC will continue cooperating with high-income countries
(i.e. the US, Canada, Japan, South-Korea and Australia) through Erasmus Mundus Join Masters,
International Credit Mobility, Jean Monnet actions and the Fulbright Schuman Programme.
DG EAC will organise three Erasmus+ Weeks in Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America/Caribbean
and Asia/Pacific/Middle East, gathering key stakeholders to promote the programme
opportunities and its results. DG EAC will also lead "Study in Europe" initiatives in India,
Moldova and Morocco. By promoting excellence in teaching and research in EU studies both in
Europe and worldwide, the Jean Monnet Actions in higher education will allow fostering
academic debates and exchange of best practices on values and democracy around the world.
The “European Voluntary Humanitarian Aid Corps”, which is part of the European
Solidarity Corps, will continue to deploy young volunteers from EU Member States and third
countries associated to the programme to contribute to humanitarian aid projects around the
world.
In the field of sport, DG EAC will continue its cooperation with countries from the Western
Balkans and the Neighbourhood East, notably via the #BeActive campaign, culminating in the
European Week of Sport and the continued support to sport capacity building actions under
Erasmus+. Moreover, DG EAC will continue its sport diplomatic dialogue with international sport
federations and, where relevant, other relevant stakeholders.
In line with the international dimension of the Culture Compass for Europe, DG EAC will
continue advancing cultural relations and dialogue with neighbouring countries, in particular the
enlargement countries. DG EAC will also continue implementing the EU–Korea Protocol on
Cultural Cooperation. Creative Europe will also support international cultural cooperation and
artist mobility.
12

General Objective 5 - Protecting our democracy,
upholding our values
Specific Objective 5.1 - Steering policies and managing
programmes in education and training, youth, sport, and
culture, promoting EU values, preparedness and resilience,
fostering a sense of European identity and enhancing
democratic participation and civic engagement
Strengthening citizenship skills, including media and digital literacy, through education (formal,
non-formal and informal), culture and sport policies is crucial for upholding EU values and
making the EU more resilient to disinformation, polarisation, and social fragmentation.
Implementing the actions outlined in the European Democracy Shield will strategically link
all EAC policies aimed at boosting societal resilience, citizen engagement, and cultural diversity.
DG EAC’s work on the Union of Skills, the European Education Area, Erasmus+ and the Culture
Compass for Europe will be central to these efforts.
Key actions in 2026 include the 2030 Roadmap on the future of digital education and skills, the
Basic Skills Support Scheme, the start of the development of guidelines for strengthening
democratic citizenship education in schools and an EU citizenship competence
framework, the EU Teachers and Trainers Agenda, the Youth Policy Dialogues on the
implementation of the European Democracy Shield and the youth ambassadors network to
discuss culture policy matters with young people as proposed in the Culture Compass, the
structured dialogue with cultural stakeholders and raising awareness on the EU’s
commitment to equity, solidarity and common values through sport (e.g. European Week of
Sport, BeActive EU Sport Awards).
Under the 2030 Roadmap, DG EAC will emphasise digital and media literacy as key to
preparedness and democratic resilience. In Q1 2026 DG EAC will launch the updated 2022
Guidelines for teachers and educators on tackling disinformation and promoting
digital literacy, providing practical support to teachers in addressing online complexity and
new forms of disinformation.
Building on the horizontal programme priority “participation in democratic life, common
values and civic engagement”, Erasmus+ and the European Solidarity Corps will foster
social and intercultural competences, critical thinking and media literacy. They will promote
European values, history and culture, and support organisations and staff in education, youth
and sport to enhance civic engagement and democratic participation. The Erasmus+ Jean
Monnet Actions will continue promoting EU teaching and critical understanding among young
people, while volunteering through the European Solidarity Corps will both strengthen local
communities and develop young people’s skills. “Enhancing intergenerational fairness and
13

solidarity” is also one of the three selected high priority areas for the 2026 action Volunteering
Teams in High Priority Areas of the European Solidarity Corps.
Building on the report on Guiding Principles on Protecting Fundamental Academic Values,
EAC will engage with the Member States in the EEA Higher Education Working Group to prepare
the ground of a respective Council Recommendation (to be adopted in 2027) as announced in
the Democracy Shield communication.
The Action Plan against cyberbullying, a key deliverable in February 2026 under the
leadership of DG CNECT, will create safer online environments for young people. The plan will
focus on minors, considering the vulnerability of certain groups of young people (e.g. people
with disabilities, LGBTIQ+ people) up to the age of 29. The plan will identify key gaps in
prevention, detection, and responses across the EU and will propose concrete actions, including
a shared definition of cyberbullying, strengthening education and support systems and
improving reporting channels. DG EAC has an important role to play in preventing and
addressing (cyber)bullying through promoting wellbeing and mental health at school, advancing
digital media literacy and digital citizenship education, combatting hate speech and offering
healthy alternatives for example through sports.
Creative Europe will continue promoting intercultural dialogue, democratic participation and a
shared European identity. In 2026, it will build on actions such as European Cooperation
Projects, Circulation of European Literary Works, European Authors Day, Culture
Moves Europe, and the Living Spaces initiative, while continuing support for flagship
initiatives including European Capitals of Culture, the European Heritage Label, and
European prizes celebrating artistic excellence, cultural diversity and EU values.
Work to strengthen the EU Youth Dialogue will continue, especially with regards to its
governance, impact and diversity. Increased alignment with the Commission policy agenda will
contribute to a stronger link with policy outcomes, as well as enhanced relevance of the EU
Youth Dialogue as a policy tool for the Commission. There will be two EU Youth Conferences in
2026; Nicosia, Cyprus, in March and Ireland (date and location still tbc). Both conferences will
play a key role in the revision of the European Youth Goals (part of the revision of the EU Youth
Strategy).
In 2026, all members of the College will hold a second round of Youth Policy Dialogues, once
again meeting with young people from across Europe. Future Youth Policy Dialogues and the
Youth Check will focus on the key initiatives of the Commission Work Programme that are most
relevant to young people, ensuring that their input directly feeds into the policymaking process.
The Youth Check represents a concrete step toward making EU policymaking more inclusive,
transparent, and responsive to young people’s needs. The Commission is already applying the
Youth Check to key initiatives planned in the 2026 Commission work programme. Young people
and youth organisations will be able to contribute through various platforms, including Youth
Policy Dialogues.
The President’s Youth Advisory Board is composed of young people from all Member
States, with representatives of candidate countries as observers. It will work in synergy with
various youth policy initiatives. Meetings will be held once or twice a year, and the Board will
come up with recommendations.
14

A key initiative for young people and the youth sector is the biennial European Youth Week
which will take place from 24 April to 1 May 2026. The 2026 edition will focus on the theme of
solidarity and fairness, with numerous events organised across Europe to showcase local and
grassroots initiatives led by Erasmus+ National Agencies and other key stakeholders.
A Eurobarometer on Youth and Democracy will be carried out in 2026. It will monitor trends
and attitudes amongst young people on topics such as youth participation, awareness of and
participation in DG EAC’s programmes and initiatives as well as views on relevance of the EU to
young people.
Cross-cutting efforts – implementation and
simplification agenda
In line with the Commission’s Communication on Implementation and Simplification (1), DG EAC
will actively contribute to the preparation of annual progress reports on simplification,
implementation and enforcement, and to the implementation dialogues under the responsibility
of Executive Vice-President Mînzatu and Commissioner Micallef. DG EAC will coordinate and
consolidate portfolio-specific evidence on simplification, implementation and enforcement in
the fields of education, youth, culture and sport and draft corresponding input for the annual
progress reports. DG EAC will also ensure consistency with programme evaluations, stakeholder
feedback and enforcement follow-up. DG EAC will also prepare the substance of
implementation dialogues, invite the relevant stakeholders and follow up on the outcome,
building on lessons learned in 2025 and ensuring that the 2026 editions reflect the strategic
priorities of the current mandate.
During the Implementation Dialogue with Commissioner Glenn Micallef on Creative Europe
Culture Cooperation Projects which took place on 18th of September 2025, participants noted
challenges with application processes and administration, which could at times be demanding
and lengthy. DG EAC will continue to work in close cooperation with the Executive Agency and
the central services (DG BUDG, DG RTD), to further simplify the application and reporting forms.
These efforts to shorten the application and reporting forms will contribute to the Commission’s
-25% / -35% burden reduction targets. Moreover, detailed guides for the applicants to help
them fill in the application forms will be developed by Creative Europe desks.
In the framework of the Commission-wide stress-test of the acquis, DG EAC has reviewed the
policy areas, programmes and initiatives under its remit. This multi-annual review was
conducted in line with the methodology applied by the Secretariat-General and takes into
consideration the Commission Strategic Plan 2025–2029, including the Commission Work
Programme (CWP) 2026, recognising that DG EAC’s responsibilities are primarily centred on
programme management, policy coordination and strategic frameworks under the Open
Method of Coordination, with a limited number of autonomous acts. Accordingly, DG EAC’s
contribution to the stress-test relies predominantly on non-legislative instruments, drawing on
existing evaluations, studies, consultations and strategic initiatives.
(1) A simpler and faster Europe: Communication on implementation and simplification
15

DG EAC conducts systematic data analytics – including AI – supported analysis starting in 2026
– on programme implementation and structured feedback collected from hundred million
participants in Erasmus+ and the European Solidarity Corps. This feedback covers participants’
learning and participation experience and includes elements relevant to delivery modalities,
administrative burden and user-friendliness. In addition, DG EAC is drawing on the Open Public
Consultation (OPC) and stakeholder consultation activities conducted in the context of the
Impact Assessment accompanying the proposals for the Erasmus+ and AgoraEU programmes
for the period 2028–2034. These analyses provide continuous, implementation-level insights
that complement formal evaluation findings.
Building on the progress achieved so far, DG EAC is preparing additional simplification
measures for the Erasmus+ National Agencies’ yearly reporting exercise 2026, to be carried out
in 2027. These measures focus on further automation and on shifting the emphasis of
reporting from data provision to analytical assessment.
In 2026, work on an improved version of the Organisations Link Explorer dashboard will
continue, in order to facilitate and simplify the work of the National Agencies in the frame of
fraud detection at application stage.
All main outputs for 2026 can be found in Annex 1 (as of p. 22), showcased under their
respective General and Specific Objectives.
16

PART 3. A modern and sustainable public
administration: outputs in 2026
The internal control framework supports sound management and decision-making. In particular,
it ensures that risks to the achievement of objectives are addressed and reduced to acceptable
levels through cost-effective controls.
DG EAC has established an internal control system tailored to its particular characteristics and
circumstances. The effective functioning of this internal control system will be assessed on an
ongoing basis throughout the year and will be subject to an annual assessment covering all
internal control principles.
A. Human resource management
DG EAC’s HR will focus on implementing the Commission’s HR strategy and corporate policies,
in close cooperation with internal communication. With the new Commission now at cruising
speed, and DG EAC serving one Executive Vice-President and two Commissioners, efficiency
gains are an imperative. HR will support the Director-General’s call for targeted adaptations of
its organisation to be fit for purpose, effective and efficient in delivering political priorities.
Following the 2025 staff opinion survey, results will be carefully analysed, and actions will be
devised accordingly, building upon actions that have been successfully carried out in 2023 and
2024 such as teams’ presentations and exchanges among staff, and between staff and senior
management.
DG EAC will support the Commission’s Diversity and Inclusion strategy, maintaining gender
balance in management and extending monitoring to executive agencies. Balanced first
appointments at middle management will remain a focus, building on the last years’
achievements and on balanced participation in management training. On 1 January 2025, 53%
of DG EAC’s middle-managers were female. Full attention will be given to implementing
corporate HR initiatives like the Management Development and Junior Professional
Programmes. The limited learning and development budget will support the building of the
teams most impacted by a reorganisation and the follow-up to the staff survey 2025, with
emphasis on promoting a respectful working environment, digital literacy and AI. Annex 2 (page
31) displays indicators to monitor the attainment of these objectives.
B. Digital transformation and data management
Digital transformation
In 2026, DG EAC will continue its digital transformation in line with the Commission Digital
Strategy, building on the 2025 achievements. Investment will focus on strengthening the
Indirect Grant Management Platform that support Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps,
notably by improving usability, reliability, and data quality for National Agencies. Core digital
services underpinning the European Solidarity Corps and the European Youth Portal will remain
17

a priority, supporting volunteer opportunities, DiscoverEU, and European Youth Week 2026 The
European Student Card Initiatives will continue its current services until the end of the funding
period, with European Student Card (ESC) being delegated to EACEA while Erasmus Without
Papers (EWP) will be managed through an Erasmus+ grant.
DG EAC will further strengthen its digital culture thanks to its “EAC Sharing Sessions,”
addressing key topics such as artificial intelligence, data, cybersecurity, digital-ready
policymaking, and effective use of Microsoft 365 tools. In parallel, DG EAC will promote
trainings offered at corporate level, notably on cybersecurity. This will equip staff with the skills
needed to work more productively and securely.
Regarding Digital Ready Policy Making, DG EAC will continue to ensure that the digital
dimension is taken into account at an early stage in the design of policy initiatives. DG EAC will
thus leverage the Digital Ready Policy Making Framework and raise awareness among policy
officers by promoting key training opportunities.
For data-driven business transformation, DG EAC will further simplify the processes
supported by its Indirect Grant Management Platform. This simplification will be accompanied
by a stronger emphasis on user experience (UX). Regarding data management, DG EAC will
focus on advancing the “Data Exchange” services, which offer National Agencies a structured
way to access and load data to the Indirect Grant Management Platform. DG EAC is therefore
implementing a data-centric strategy step by step. AI will also be leveraged for operational
efficiency in areas like AI for developers and eLoqui for training videos.
In 2026, DG EAC will strive to maintain its systems using state-of-the-art technologies to
ensure a seamless digital environment. DG EAC will foster reuse by leveraging the Reusable
Solutions Platform (e.g. Compass, EU Login, eUI, EU Survey, etc.). Open source remains a
cornerstone of DG EAC’s digital transformation, with support for both the adoption of open-
source tools (e.g. PostgreSQL) and contributions to open-source projects (e.g. Drupal). DG EAC
will also pursue its cloud transformation journey launched in 2024, with the ambition that 60%
of DG EAC systems will use cloud infrastructure by the end of 2026.
Concerning secure, green, and resilient infrastructure, DG EAC will rely on DIGIT
infrastructure and services. Cybersecurity will remain a key priority. In line with the EC
Cybersecurity Strategy 2025–2026, DG EAC will raise staff cyber-awareness (cf. digital culture),
ensure compliance with the cybersecurity risk management, governance, and control
framework, and strengthen security processes, notably by improving vulnerability management.
Data, information & knowledge management
In 2026, DG EAC will continue to position data and artificial intelligence as strategic assets
across the policy and programme cycle, in line with the EAC Data and AI Strategy and the
Commission’s Digital Strategy. The objective is to consolidate DG EAC as a data-driven and AI-
enabled organisation where reliable data, responsible algorithms, and automated analytics
systematically support policy design, programme management, monitoring, and evaluation. This
will reinforce simplification, efficiency, and evidence-based decision-making across all policy
areas.
18

DG EAC will maintain its overall data and AI maturity at Established level in 2026. The
progressive deployment of the EAC Data and AI Platform will be central in linking programme,
financial, and policy data to advanced analytics and AI-assisted insight generation.
Data management
Within its Established maturity level, data management efforts will focus on stronger
integration, interoperability, and automation to ensure a unified, trusted, integrated data layer
for corporate reporting and performance monitoring. These improvements will streamline
processes, reduce duplication, and enhance analytical depth.
Data and AI governance and responsibilities
DG EAC will move from Established to Advanced maturity by fully operationalising its Data
Governance Framework, clarifying data ownership and stewardship, and embedding
responsibility and transparency. Standardised procedures for assessing AI-related risks will
ensure alignment with corporate requirements and principles of trustworthy, explainable, and
secure AI use.
Data quality on policy and programme performance
Data quality will be reinforced through automated validation, systematic metadata
management, and application of FAIR principles, improving the accuracy, coherence, and
reusability of programme and policy datasets. This will support more robust reporting and more
reliable evidence for evaluation.
Data and AI literacy
DG EAC will also expand its data and AI literacy programme through targeted capacity-building
for headquarters, National Agencies, and EACEA to move from Established to Advanced
maturity. Training will focus on visual analytics, evaluation-ready datasets, and responsible AI
practices, enabling full use of the EAC Data and AI Platform and contributing to simplified,
higher-quality reporting and more meaningful insights into programme and policy results.
Data protection
DG EAC will continue monitoring the implementation of the Commission's Data Protection
Action Plan, reporting annually to the senior management. Different awareness raising
activities will be organised: meetings of data protection network, dissemination of course
offers, intranet publications, and data protection quizzes. DG EAC will ensure compliance with
the obligations concerning record keeping by means of creating new records for the new
DG EAC processing activities, update the existing records on a bi-annual basis, in accordance
with Commission corporate policies. The inventory of processing agreements with external
processors (contracts with various service providers and contribution agreements with National
Agencies) will be updated regularly (once every six months). The updated procedure for data
subject rights (approved by the Data Steering Committee) will be used together with the
corporate templates in order to reply to all data subjects received directly by DG EAC or
transmitted by DPO.
19

A baseline value of 90% will be assigned for the compliance indicator in 2026. This was
calculated as: percentage of staff trained on data protection compliance combined with the
percentage of public records of processing operations reviewed within the last two years.
C. Sound financial management
Targets on the error rate will be maintained as per Annex 2 (page 35) with a risk at payments
and closure of less than 2%.
In 2026, DG EAC will continue working towards optimising financial management processes
using SUMMA and other corporate financial management tools, such as eProcurement or ABAC
Assets. The tools are still under development and improving gradually; DG EAC will maintain
focusing on adjusting the financial workflows and procedures to the new environment and
continue recreating operational financial reports using the new data structure imposed by the
new systems. DG EAC will continue fine-tuning the new accounting control plan established
under the new accounting control framework. DG EAC will also continue exploring together with
central services and other DGs to find the adequate combination of corporate tools, in
particular to fill functional gaps in the financial software related to indirect management, which
would allow it to manage its operations with National Agencies more efficiently.
Beyond financial and accounting processes, DG EAC will continue to pursue a proactive and
strategically coordinated approach to budget management in 2026. Building on the strong
results achieved so far and on the ongoing budget implementation strategy for 2025–2026,
the Directorate will aim to ensure continued excellence in budget execution, accurate
forecasting, and credible financial planning within a constrained budgetary context under direct
and indirect management mode for all its programmes and actions. The priority will be to
maintain the high absorption of EAC programmes while safeguarding budgetary discipline and
flexibility to respond to evolving policy needs. Close coordination with Executive Agencies and
National Agencies will remain essential to ensure accurate forecasts, optimal management of
financial workflow, and smooth implementation of both commitment and payment
appropriations.
D. Fraud risk management
In line with the Commission Anti-Fraud Strategy (CAFS) and its 2023 action plan, DG EAC
adopted on 21 November 2024 an updated Anti-Fraud Strategy 2025-2027 which includes a
revised action plan to take account of the control strategy for the 2021-2027 programmes. The
revised action plan emphasises greater business intelligence and risk assessment regarding
beneficiary profiles. More specifically, as regards action point I.2, DG EAC started to develop in
2025 a reinforced monitoring tool in the Project Management Module to ensure that excluded
or high-risk entities are closely monitored by the National Agencies. This tool is expected to be
in production in February 2026. In addition, the multiple organisations tool (action point 1.1)
was finalised end 2025. In 2026, DG EAC will draft guidance notes for the National Agencies to
ensure that both the multiple organisations reporting tool and the reinforced monitoring tool
are used properly. In 2026, DG EAC will perform an internal review of anti-fraud safeguards in
20

National Agency Management, including conflict of interest (action point 3.1) by including it in
the scope of the monitoring and supervisory activities. DG EAC will contribute to the
implementation of the CAFS Action Plan, and will continue its cooperation with OLAF, notably by
participating to the Fraud Prevention and Detection Network meetings.
Please see Annex 2 (ANNEX 2: Performance tables – A modern and sustainable public
administration), part D Fraud Risk Management, page 36.

• reducing GHG emissions linked to staff business and expert’s travel while promoting
sustainable travel actions (=e.g. reducing emissions with 50% for 2019-2030,
baseline 2019: 284 087 CO2/kg (source: Mips report)) for official missions,
• using more efficient and sustainable building and office space while continuing to
participate in the annual BEST energy saving actions (summer/winter actions),
• increasing green mobility for commuting,
• optimising IT operations and assets etc.
B. Staff Participation and Communication by
• publishing EMAS/greening corporate campaigns and related articles provided by
central services,
• re-publish EC Guidelines for sustainable events on EAC’s Intranet.
In addition, DG EAC will put in place a new "EAC Greening Action Plan" covering the period
2026-2028.
